problem: Embodied AI simulation environments are hand-designed (iTHOR, RoboTHOR), 3D-scanned (HM3D) or generated by hard-coded procedural rules (ProcTHOR, limited to bathroom/bedroom/kitchen/living room), so they cover few scene and object types. Text-to-3D scene methods (Text2Room, SceneScape, Text2NeRF) produce distorted, non-interactive meshes. LLM layout methods like LayoutGPT, which output absolute coordinates, produce collisions and out-of-boundary objects.
motivation: Agent generalization depends on training-environment diversity. Existing ObjectNav benchmarks cover only household scenes, with 16 object types across RoboTHOR, ProcTHOR and HM3D combined, so agents cannot handle novel scene types such as gyms or music rooms. The paper's observation is that LLMs like GPT-4 hold commonsense priors about what a scene contains and how it is arranged. Pairing those priors with a large asset library (Objaverse) and a proper layout solver could produce interactive AI2-THOR scenes of arbitrary type from a text prompt.
key_idea: Use GPT-4 as a multi-module scene designer whose outputs are grounded into AI2-THOR: floor plan, materials, doors/windows, object proposals retrieved from about 51K Objaverse assets, and spatial relational constraints that a DFS/MILP solver turns into collision-free layouts. The generated scenes are then used to fine-tune ObjectNav agents for unseen scene types.
insight: Letting the LLM emit qualitative spatial relations and delegating the numbers to a constraint solver is much more reliable than having the LLM output coordinates. In the human-ranked layout ablation (Table 1, MRR), Constraint scores 0.706 vs Edge 0.645, Random 0.369 and LayoutGPT-style Absolute 0.364; Absolute is no better than random because of collisions and boundary errors. For navigation, the ProcTHOR-10K-pretrained agent is near random on novel scene types (4.11 vs 3.71 SR), which shows object coverage is the first bottleneck. Holding assets fixed, +Holodeck beats +Objaverse (ProcTHOR layouts populated with the same Holodeck-selected assets): 20.40 vs 17.02 SR and 0.127 vs 0.093 SPL. This indicates that realistic, commonsense object placement also transfers to expert-designed scenes. The gains are concentrated in Office, Daycare and Music Room and absent in Gym and Arcade.
method: Floor & Wall Module: GPT-4 outputs each room as a rectangle (4 vertex coordinates, 3-8 m sides, ≤48 m²) plus floor/wall material descriptions and wall height. Materials are chosen by OpenCLIP ViT-L/14 matching against 236 material images × 148 Matplotlib colors.

Doorway & Window Module: separate LLM queries propose room connections (doorframe/doorway/open, single 1 m or double 2 m, door style) and windows (wall direction, fixed/hung/slider, size, quantity, base height). CLIP retrieves from 40 door and 21 window assets.

Object Selection Module: GPT-4 proposes floor, wall and on-top small objects with description, size (cm) and quantity. Retrieval over 51,464 assets (Objaverse subset annotated by GPT-4V, plus ProcTHOR assets) maximizes M = 100·CLIP(render, text) + 1·SBERT(text, text) − 10·mean bbox size discrepancy.

Constraint-based Layout Design: GPT-4 assigns each object 10 constraint types in 5 groups (global edge/middle; near/far; in front of/side of/above/on top of; center aligned; face to) and picks an anchor object. A grid-based DFS solver places objects autoregressively over 4 discrete rotations, rejecting placements that break the hard constraints (no collision, inside room). It counts soft-constraint satisfaction, runs for 30 s and returns the layout satisfying the most constraints. A Gurobi MILP solver is an alternative.
Wall/small object placement: wall objects are placed via an 'above (floor object)' relation plus height. Small objects are placed on LLM-chosen surfaces with AI2-THOR RandomSpawn.

Objaverse → AI2-THOR import: GPT-4V annotates category, WordNet synset (used as ObjectNav type), dimensions, mass, front view and placement flags. The pipeline reduces meshes, generates visibility points, builds convex-decomposition colliders, compresses textures, and caches/unloads assets at runtime.

ObjectNav adaptation + NoveltyTHOR: 100 scenes per novel scene type are generated from the scene name and paraphrases. A ProcTHOR-10K-pretrained EmbCLIP (CLIP CNN + GRU) ObjectNav agent is fine-tuned on them for 50M steps and evaluated on 10 artist-designed scenes (Office, Daycare, Music Room, Gym, Arcade; 92 object types).

setting.backbone: Navigation policy: EmbCLIP ObjectNav agent (CLIP CNN visual encoder + GRU), pretrained on ProcTHOR-10K and fine-tuned. Scene generation: GPT-4 (gpt-4-1106-preview, frozen), GPT-4V for asset annotation, OpenCLIP ViT-L/14 and SBERT for retrieval.
setting.training_data: ProcTHOR-10K pretraining (~400M steps, 16 object categories), then fine-tuning for 50M steps on 100 Holodeck-generated scenes per target scene type (5 types: Office, Daycare, Music Room, Gym, Arcade). Scenes use a library of 51,464 annotated Objaverse + ProcTHOR assets. Each model trains about 1 day on 8 Quadro RTX 8000 GPUs.
setting.observation: egocentric RGB (EmbCLIP ObjectNav agent; sensor suite not detailed in paper)
setting.action_space: discrete AI2-THOR navigation actions (not detailed in paper)

numbers.backbone: EmbCLIP ObjectNav (CLIP CNN + GRU), ProcTHOR-10K pretrained
numbers.extra: Fine-tuned 50M steps on 100 GPT-4/Holodeck-generated scenes per target scene type, prompted with scene name + paraphrases. Paper calls this 'zero-shot' because no human-built scenes of the target types are used. Checkpoint selected on its own generated validation scenes. NoveltyTHOR has 10 artist-designed scenes, 2 per type; episode count not stated. SPL printed as fraction (e.g. 0.127) and converted to 0-100 here.

numbers_note: The only navigation results are Table 2 (ObjectNav on the new NoveltyTHOR benchmark: 10 scenes, episode count not given). The human-evaluation results appear only as pie charts, CLIP-score bar charts and per-scene-type score plots (Figs.), with a few percentages quoted in text. The layout ablation is Table 1 (Mean Reciprocal Rank: Constraint 0.706, Edge 0.645, Random 0.369, Absolute 0.364 average). These are not navigation benchmarks and are left out of 'numbers'.
results: On NoveltyTHOR ObjectNav, fine-tuning on Holodeck scenes lifts the ProcTHOR-10K-pretrained agent from 4.11 SR / 0.015 SPL (near the random agent's 3.71 / 0.037) to 20.40 SR / 0.127 SPL. It also beats the asset-matched +Objaverse baseline (17.02 / 0.093), with the largest gains on Office, Daycare and Music Room. In a 680-participant human study, annotators preferred Holodeck over ProcTHOR on residential scenes (Asset Selection 59.8%, Layout Coherence 56.9%, Overall 64.4%). Holodeck exceeded ProcTHOR's residential average on 28 of 52 MIT scene types. The constraint-based layout wins the MRR ablation (0.706 vs 0.364 for LLM absolute coordinates).
limitations: Struggles with scenes that need complex layouts (e.g., restaurant) or assets missing from Objaverse (e.g., dental x-ray machine). Rooms are rectangles only, objects have 4 axis-aligned rotations, and scene types needing special structures (swimming pool, subway) were excluded.

The navigation evaluation is small (10 artist scenes). Gains are inconsistent (+Holodeck ≤ +Objaverse on Gym and Arcade), absolute success stays low (~20%), and the policy is fine-tuned for each known target scene type.
Relies on the closed GPT-4 / GPT-4V API (~$0.2 and ~3 min per room). Generation inherits LLM cultural biases, which prompting only partially mitigates.
compares_to: ProcTHOR (scene generation and ProcTHOR-10K-pretrained ObjectNav agent)
